Cc: Tim Hall <tim.hall@cloudmetrics.com>

Subject: Re: Multi-region DR SLO review (CloudMetrics production)

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the call this morning. Legal flagged a hard requirement for our procurement: the platform must provide a documented multi-region failover that meets RTO <= 30s and RPO <= 1s for our production ingestion and inference endpoints. That requirement is written into our procurement checklist and drives our board sign-off.

Before we move to contract redlines, can you confirm whether Redwood can meet those RTO/RPO numbers in our standard Hosted tier, or if not, what the incremental commitments and pricing would be to reach them (e.g., dedicated warm pools, guaranteed pre-warmed KV caches, multi-region active-active with sync)?

A few clarifying points from our side:
- Failure mode we care about: full regional AZ+region outage (not just single AZ).
- Traffic profile: sustained 300 qps, spiky peaks to 800 qps for bursts up to 10 minutes.
- Observability needed: per-request latency breakdowns, token-level traces, and post-failover replay logs.

Can you outline options and an expected timeline to operationalize? Legal asked for a short write-up we can attach to our procurement packet by EOD next Tues.

Appreciate it —
Erin
Principal Infrastructure Manager
CloudMetrics Inc.

Subject: Fwd: Multi-region DR SLO review (CloudMetrics production)

Laura / Grace —
Forwarding Erin's ask. Short: CloudMetrics is asking for RTO <=30s and RPO <=1s across region failures for their production traffic (300qps sustained, spikes to 800qps). Legal wants a one-page confirmation of our capability or a clearly scoped exception + pricing.

Quick thoughts:
- Hosted default: cold warm-up and KV-cache population make <30s at scale very hard unless we pre-warm dedicated capacity per-account and keep KV caches warm (costly).
- Dedicated pools with always-on warm instances + prefix caching could reliably hit RTO ~60–120s depending on model size and sequence lengths; getting to 30s is extreme for worst-case region failure.
- RPO ~1s implies synchronous replication of state (user-owned KV, logs, or streaming checkpoints). Our typical design is best-effort cross-region replication for KV caches and asynchronous storage for logs; achieving sub-second RPO would require changes.

Can you put together two options (minimal operational exception + premium engineering option) with bullet cost estimates and the runbook for failover? I'll propose language to legal that preserves our standard SLA but allows a documented variance for this account.

Marcus
Head of Partnerships (fwd from inbox)
Redwood Inference

Marcus —

Attached is a concise two-option proposal I drafted: one is an 'operational variance' (fast path, lower cost, some measured risk) and the other is a 'guaranteed premium' package that would require Dedicated warm pools + synchronous replication for critical metadata. Summary below (will attach cost workbook):

Option A — Operational variance (lower cost)
- Commitment: Failover target ~120s RTO for region-to-region recovery (99.9% availability across two regions).
- RPO: best-effort; expected RPO <= 5s for inference request state via low-latency cross-region replication, not guaranteed sub-second.
- Mitigations: reserve priority routing + active health checks, pre-provision small warm pool per region (configurable), runbook with 2-person page and automated traffic-shift script.
- Tradeoffs: transient token replays may be necessary for some sessions; some dependent features (session-based KV) will experience eventual consistency.

Option B — Premium guaranteed package
- Commitment: RTO <= 30s, RPO <= 1s for specified endpoints.
- Requirements: Dedicated capacity with always-on warm instances sized for peak (800 qps), synchronous replicated KV across regions (engineering change + audit), 24/7 on-call SLA with runbook drills and quarterly DR tests — delivered as a paid add-on (annual commitment).
- Financial: materially higher (see workbook) — largely driven by reserved GPU capacity and networking/replication costs.
- Legal: must include explicit SLA amendment with targeted credits for missed failover objectives and a joint runbook acceptance clause.

Recommendation: Start with Option A to keep the purchase moving and include an explicit roadmap and offline acceptance criteria for Option B. That gives CloudMetrics immediate protections while giving us time to scope the engineering work for sub-30s guarantees.

I've attached: proposed-dr-slo-delta.pdf and warm-pool-cost-estimate.xlsx and a short draft runbook (runbook-failover-summary.docx).

If you want, I can write the short 1‑page confirmation Erin needs by EOD Tues and call out the variance language we propose.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Erin —

Thanks again for outlining CloudMetrics' procurement requirement. We've reviewed and put together two pragmatic paths you can attach to your packet. High-level summary (see attached for detail):

1) Option A — Operational variance (recommended short term)
- SLOs: We will commit to a documented multi-region failover process with an operational RTO target of 120 seconds and an availability objective of 99.9% across the protected region pair.
- RPO: best-effort cross-region replication; expected RPO <= 5s for inference metadata and logs, not a contractual sub-second guarantee.
- Controls: prioritized routing on Redwood's control plane during incidents, a pre-provisioned warm pool per region (configurable size), dedicated runbook with manual and automated traffic-shift steps, and a post-failover reconciliation report within 4 business hours.
- Pricing: nominal monthly surcharge for the reserved warm pool + incident priority queue (estimate attached).

2) Option B — Premium guaranteed package
- SLOs: Contract amendment to guarantee RTO <= 30s and RPO <= 1s for named endpoints.
- Requirements: Dedicated capacity sized to your peak, synchronous replication of critical state, quarterly DR exercises with acceptance criteria, and 24/7 on‑call coverage.
- Pricing: annual reserved commitment required; pricing estimate in attached workbook.

Next steps I'd propose:
- If you need something immediately for procurement, accept Option A and we'll provide the 1‑page confirmation for your packet by EOD Tue.
- If CloudMetrics wants contractual sub-30s guarantees, we should open a short scoping engagement (SOW) to size and instrument Option B. That will include a technical plan, security review, and legal amendment draft.

I'll attach a one-page confirmation and a proposed SLA variance clause for your legal team to review. Please let me know which path you prefer or if you want us to scope Option B in parallel.

Best,
Marcus Lin
